bibliography.note: Saila, S. B. 1956. Estimates of the minimum size-limit for maximum yield and production of chain pickerel, Esox niger LeSueur, in Rhode Island. Limnology and Oceanography 1(3): 195–201 — matches. Drop '(not obtained)' from the entry

claims.claim: an estimate from age frequencies in two Rhode Island ponds, an exploited and an unexploited one
claims.location: p. 195 (PDF p. 1), Mortality components; p. 196 (PDF p. 2), Table 1 and text
claims.quote: chain pickerel killed during the chemical reclamation of a 320-acre pond
claims.conditions: unexploited: Larkin Pond, 44 acres, South Kingston RI, fyke net fished 20 days, no fishing for several years; exploited: Wallum Lake, 320 acres, 'partly in Rhode Island and partly in Massachusetts', fish killed in a chemical reclamation; total mortality from the weighted geometric mean of age frequencies (Rounsefell & Everhart 1953)
claims.note: the exploited water straddles the RI–MA line

claims.claim: no catch-curve, tagging or mark–recapture survival estimate for chain pickerel in a northeastern lake exists or was obtained; Saila 1956 could not be read
claims.source_value: Saila 1956 is such an estimate and is now read: weighted annual survival 0.54 (annual mortality 0.46, instantaneous 0.61 = natural mortality) in unexploited Larkin Pond, ages IV–VIII; 0.45 (mortality 0.55, instantaneous 0.79) in exploited Wallum Lake, ages II–VI; fishing mortality p = 0.18 (annual 0.16)
claims.conditions: age-frequency (catch-curve) method; Larkin n = 41 aged fish (8 younger fish dropped), Wallum n = 52 (24 age-I fish dropped); samples were 15 and 28 % of the estimated population ≥ 10 in TL; scale ages, uncertainty rising with age ('tends to overestimate survival rate'); dominant year classes assumed absent. Unweighted values: Larkin s 0.50, Wallum s 0.30
claims.note: The sentences saying no such estimate was found should now cite Saila: natural mortality (instantaneous) 0.61 yr⁻¹, adult survival without fishing 0.54. That sits at the top of the paper's life-history M range (0.24–0.66) and just below the notes' adult survival of 0.55–0.70 for a lightly fished Maine population

notes: The paper repeatedly says this study 'could not be read'; it is now read and gives the only northeastern pickerel survival estimate found: annual survival 0.54 unfished (Larkin Pond, 44 ac) and 0.45 fished (Wallum Lake, 320 ac), natural mortality 0.61 yr⁻¹ (instantaneous). Other useful values: Rhode Island growth from 257 fish in 32 ponds, mean fork length (back-calculated, Lee's method, 37.7-mm intercept; Table 4, p. 200, read on the page image) at age I 167 mm (28 g), II 267 (120 g), III 316 (200 g), IV 358 (284 g), V 405 (430 g), VI 436 (554 g), VII 472 (715 g), VIII 515 mm (953 g); Table 4 also uses natural mortality q = 0.6 yr⁻¹ throughout; length–weight log W = −5.5101 + 3.1304 log FL (W g, FL mm), p. 198; best minimum size limit ~11–12 in TL; yield < 39 % of production; Lee's phenomenon detected in back-calculated age-I lengths.
